Excellent. Now I have all the information I need. Let me prepare the comprehensive report:

---

## Current Shape (5-bullet summary)

1. **Two-layer structure**: Industry (12 sectors, ~50 tools across them) and Public (5 domains with 6-8 PDTs each, ~50+ tools). Total ~108 tools, ~149 MCPs (41 real MCPs + placeholder padding). Renders as responsive grid of cards.

2. **Drill-driven navigation**: State lives in URL query params (`layer`, `primary`, `secondary`, `status`, `view`). Default landing shows *all groups at once*. User can drill to a sector/domain (sets `primary`) or a PDT (sets `primary + secondary`). Drilling filters the visible cards client-side; no fetch needed.

3. **No truncation by default**: In "no drill" (default) state, **every MCP is visible** — all 149 tiles render fully in an auto-fit grid. The cards themselves never truncate MCPs; they all display inline. The side panel (ToolDetailPanel) opens as an overlay but doesn't hide anything in the main view.

4. **Information hiding happens in two places**:
   - **CardHeader** click triggers drill (emits `@drill`, changes route)
   - **McpTile** click opens side panel (emits `pick`, doesn't navigate)
   - MCP **names/blurbs are visible directly in tiles** in the main view: compact mode shows just slug + status dot; full mode (rarely used) shows more.
   - The **ToolDetailPanel (side panel, 440px wide)** reveals: tool name, MCP name, full blurb, tags, deps count, endpoint URI, owner context, and downstream MCPs (illustrative sample).

5. **View modes**: "panorama" (grid of cards, drill-friendly, default) vs. "list" (3-column status layout per group, no drill support). Switching view mode clears drill state implicitly (status filter stays).

---

## Per-Component Findings

### PanoramaView.vue (lines 1–61)
**Role**: Top-level wrapper for the "panorama" view mode. Responsible for layout grid selection and event routing.

**Template structure**:
- Renders `LayerSummary` (stats card) at top
- Below it, a responsive CSS grid: `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(320px|520px, 1fr))` depending on layer
  - Industry layer: 320px minimum card width
  - Public layer: 520px minimum (wider because PDTs add sub-grids)
- Loops over `groups` prop and renders either `SectorCard` or `DomainCard` per group

**Drill mechanics**:
- Emits `@drill` when a group header is clicked (forwarded from CardHeader → drillTo)
- `LayerSummary` also emits `@drill` when "top 3 by release%" buttons are clicked (lines 156)
- No truncation: all groups render simultaneously in the grid

**MCP visibility**:
- MCPs render as tiles inside each card, no hiding. Scroll happens at page level only, not card level.

---

### LayerSummary.vue (lines 1–169)
**Role**: Statistics dashboard at the top showing layer-wide health, not a drill trigger for primary use.

**Template structure** (lines 39–168):
- Large fixed-width grid: `grid-template-columns: minmax(260px, 1.3fr) repeat(3, minmax(120px, 1fr)) minmax(220px, 1.4fr)`
- Left column: Big `{{ stats.activePct }}%` display + stacked bar chart (lines 44–94)
- Three center columns: Clickable buttons for Released / Dev / No MCP counts (lines 98–141)
- Right column: "Top 3 by release %" with drill buttons (lines 144–167)

**Drill mechanics** (lines 150–165):
```vue
<button @click="emit('drill', g.key)">{{ title(g) }}</button>
```
Each of the top 3 groups is a clickable button that drills into that group. This is **secondary drill entry point** (primary entry point is card headers in SectorCard/DomainCard).

**Data shown**:
- Status indicator bar (color-coded by released/dev/none)
- Exact counts by status (not truncated; all visible)
- Rollup percentage for the layer

---

### SectorCard.vue (lines 1–29)
**Role**: Industry-layer group card wrapper. Hosts CardHeader + ToolMcpsCard grid.

**Template structure** (lines 16–29):
```vue
<article class="bg-(--color-card) border rounded-xl p-3.5 flex flex-col gap-3">
  <CardHeader @drill="emit('drill', props.group.key)" />
  <div class="bg-(--color-bg) rounded-lg p-2.5 flex flex-col gap-1.5">
    <ToolMcpsCard v-for="tool in group.items" ... />
  </div>
</article>
```

**Drill mechanics**:
- CardHeader emits `@drill` when the sector name is clicked
- No limit on tools rendered; `v-for` renders all tools in the sector
- No max-height or scroll container inside the card; tools stack vertically

**MCP visibility**:
- Each `ToolMcpsCard` renders all MCPs for that tool inline (wrapped in flex-wrap)
- No truncation: **all MCPs visible at once**

---

### DomainCard.vue (lines 1–29)
**Role**: Public-layer group card wrapper. Adds PDT sub-grouping via `PdtBlock` components.

**Template structure** (lines 16–29):
```vue
<article class="bg-(--color-card) border rounded-xl p-3.5 flex flex-col gap-3">
  <CardHeader @drill="emit('drill', props.group.key)" />
  <div class="grid gap-2.5" style="grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(260px, 1fr))">
    <PdtBlock v-for="pdt in group.pdts" ... />
  </div>
</article>
```

**Drill mechanics**:
- CardHeader emits `@drill` when the domain name is clicked
- PDTs are in a nested auto-fit grid (min 260px per PDT)
- **Important**: Clicking a PDT header in `PdtBlock` does NOT drill; PDTs are purely layout containers. Drill only happens from the domain-level CardHeader.

**MCP visibility**:
- All PDTs and their tools render inside the domain card
- No truncation at domain or PDT level

---

### PdtBlock.vue (lines 1–42)
**Role**: Public-layer PDT subgroup. Contains a header + stacked ToolMcpsCard list.

**Template structure** (lines 24–41):
```vue
<section class="bg-(--color-bg) rounded-lg px-2.5 py-2.5 flex flex-col gap-2">
  <header class="flex items-baseline justify-between gap-2 px-0.5">
    <span>{{ title }}</span>
    <span>{{ mcpCount }}</span>  <!-- Just a label, not clickable -->
  </header>
  <div class="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
    <ToolMcpsCard v-for="tool in pdt.items" ... />
  </div>
</section>
```

**Key detail**: The header (lines 26–30) is **not a button**; it's a static `<span>`. PDTs do not drill.

**MCP visibility**:
- All tools in the PDT render vertically (no truncation)
- `mcpCount` is a static count; no "show more" pattern

---

### ToolMcpsCard.vue (lines 1–72)
**Role**: Single tool + all its MCPs, rendered as a card with tool name + inline MCP tiles.

**Template structure** (lines 41–72):
```vue
<article class="bg-(--color-card) border rounded-lg shadow... px-3 py-2.5">
  <header class="flex items-center gap-2 min-w-0">
    <span class="font-serif text-[13.5px]">{{ toolName }}</span>
    <span v-if="realMcpCount > 1" class="text-[9px]">×{{ realMcpCount }}</span>
    <span class="size-[6px] rounded-full">{{ rollupStatus dot }}</span>
  </header>
  <div class="flex flex-wrap gap-1.5">
    <McpTile v-for="mcp in tool.mcps" ... />
  </div>
</article>
```

**Drill mechanics**:
- Tool name is not clickable (static text)
- Emits `@pick` when an MCP tile is clicked

**MCP visibility** (lines 60–69):
- **All MCPs render in a flex-wrap container** — no truncation, no "show N of M" pattern
- Even if a tool has many MCPs, they all wrap and display (Slack sidebar-style; wraps to next line)
- Status dot is tool-level rollup; individual MCPs have their own status

**No real truncation here.** The flex-wrap layout ensures every tile is visible if you scroll the page.

---

### McpTile.vue (lines 1–102)
**Role**: Individual MCP cell — the smallest renderable unit on the panorama.

**Template structure** (lines 74–101):
```vue
<NuxtLink v-if="isReleased && mcp.extensionSlug" ... >
  <span>{{ displayName }}</span>
  <span v-if="showDeps">· {{ mcp.depsCount }}</span>
  <ChevronRight />
</NuxtLink>
<button v-else ...>
  <span>{{ displayName }}</span>
  <span v-if="showDeps">· {{ mcp.depsCount }}</span>
</button>
```

**Click behavior** (lines 64–71):
- If released + has extensionSlug: click → NuxtLink to `/extensions/<slug>`
- Else: button → emits `pick` → opens side panel
- Either way, **does not drill**; stays in panorama view

**Data shown**:
- MCP display name (slug, or placeholder "—")
- Deps count if ≥ 10 (line 27: `showDeps = depsCount >= 10`)
- Status color (compact pill: `px-2 py-[3px] text-[11px]` or larger `px-2.5 py-[5px] text-[12px]`)
- Hovering released MCPs lifts them slightly (line 61: `hover:-translate-y-px`)

**Key point**: Names and blurbs **are NOT hidden**. The tile shows the name inline. Full blurb is in the side panel (ToolDetailPanel), but the name is visible here.

---

### CardHeader.vue (lines 1–34)
**Role**: Clickable group header (sector or domain name + MCP count).

**Template structure** (lines 13–33):
```vue
<header class="flex items-baseline justify-between gap-3 min-w-0">
  <h3>
    <button
      class="flex items-baseline gap-2 min-w-0 ... cursor-pointer"
      :title="t('mcpPanorama.card.drillIn', { name: displayTitle })"
      @click="emit('drill')"
    >
      <span class="font-serif text-[18px] ... truncate">{{ displayTitle }}</span>
      <span class="font-mono text-[11px]">{{ group.stats.total }}</span>
    </button>
  </h3>
  <span class="font-mono text-[11px] tabular-nums">
    <span>{{ group.stats.counts.released }}</span>/{{ group.stats.total }}
  </span>
</header>
```

**Drill mechanics**:
- The group title is a clickable button (line 17–19)
- Emits `drill` event with no payload (parent reads `props.group.key`)
- **This is the primary drill entry point for sectors/domains**

**Data shown**:
- Group display name (truncated if long)
- Total MCP count in group
- Released count and total (right side)

---

### ToolDetailPanel.vue (lines 1–342)
**Role**: Fixed 440px-wide side panel that slides in from the right when an MCP is "picked".

**Structure** (lines 149–342):
- Fixed positioning: `fixed top-0 right-0 bottom-0 bg-(--color-card) overflow-hidden z-30`
- Slides in/out: `transition-[width] duration-300 ease-out`, width toggles between `0` and `440px`
- Content organized in sections with borders:
  - Header + close button (lines 156–197)
  - Status description (lines 201–207)
  - Tags row (lines 211–219)
  - Meta grid (lines 223–256): deps count, owner, endpoint URI
  - Sibling MCPs in same tool (lines 260–283)
  - Downstream MCPs (illustrative, lines 287–313)
  - Footer buttons (lines 317–340)

**What information appears here** (that's NOT visible in the main panorama):
- **Full MCP name** (line 183: `{{ mcpName }}`)
- **Full blurb** (line 197: `{{ mcpBlurb }}`)
- Status description (full i18n string, lines 201–207)
- Tags (inline pills, lines 215–219)
- Deps count (line 229)
- Endpoint URI / slug (line 243)
- Owner context + layer badge (lines 162–169)
- Downstream MCPs (sample of 5, lines 294–312)
- Links to marketplace and docs

**Key hiding pattern**:
- MCP **names are visible in the panorama** (McpTile shows slug)
- But the **full blurb is only in the side panel** (lines 40–42 compute it, line 197 render it)
- In the panorama, ToolMcpsCard shows tool name + MCP count; McpTile shows status color + name
- **Status indicators (released/dev/none) are visible in tiles** — colored pills directly in the panorama

**No drilling from this panel**:
- Switching MCPs via sibling list (lines 268–283) emits `switch-mcp` (not a drill)
- Close button resets to panorama (line 192: `@click="emit('close'"`)

---

### GroupedListView.vue (lines 1–134)
**Role**: Alternative "list" view mode (not default). Shows a 3-column grid per group/PDT with MCPs sorted by status.

**Layout** (lines 71–133):
- Per group/PDT section (industrial or per-PDT in public layer)
- Header with title + status bar (lines 74–100)
- Main grid: 3 columns (lines 103), one per status (none, dev, released)
- Each column lists `ToolCard` components (one tool per card; MCPs not separated)

**Important**: This view mode **does not support drill**. It flattens all MCPs into status buckets, so there's no primary/secondary grouping.

**MCP visibility**:
- All MCPs visible in one view (3-column grid)
- No truncation; scrolls vertically if needed
- Clicking on an MCP opens the side panel (emits `pick`)

---

## Where is Information Hidden Today?

### Landing state (`/mcp/panorama` with no query params)

**Visible**:
- All ~149 MCPs rendered as tiles in the panorama grid
- All sector/domain cards expanded
- All PDT sub-cards (public layer) expanded
- Tool names visible in ToolMcpsCard headers
- MCP names visible as tile labels
- Status colors (released/dev/none) visible as pill backgrounds
- Rollup status dot visible in tool headers
- All counts visible (total MCPs per group, released/total in headers)

**Hidden**:
- Full MCP blurbs (only in side panel)
- Tags (only in side panel)
- Endpoint URIs (only in side panel)
- Downstream dependencies visualization (only in side panel)
- Owner context detail beyond the primary group name (in side panel)

### After drilling (e.g., `?primary=wireless`)

**Still visible**:
- All MCPs *in that sector/domain* (filtered client-side)
- Same tile structure
- CardHeader now shows "drill back" button context (via LayerSummary + SectionHeader breadcrumb logic)

**Still hidden**: Same as above (blurbs, tags, endpoint, deps)

### After opening side panel (e.g., click an MCP tile)

**Now visible (in side panel)**:
- Full MCP name
- Full blurb
- Tags
- Status description
- Endpoint URI (if released)
- Owner detail (domain + PDT or sector)
- Deps count
- Sibling MCPs in same tool (all of them, in scrollable list)
- Downstream MCPs (illustrative sample)

**Main view unchanged**: Panorama still shows all groups/MCPs; side panel overlays without hiding anything.

---

## Data Volume

Extracted from `mcp-landscape.ts` (519 lines):

**Industry layer**:
- 12 sectors (lines 73–86)
- ~50 tools distributed across sectors
- Example sector distribution (inferred from data):
  - Wireless: ~7 tools (5G-Sim, RadioPlan, SpectrumMgr, BeamOpt, AntennaCAD, RANConfig, FieldTest)
  - Datacom: ~5 tools (RouteForge, PacketLens, ConfigPilot, TopoMap, NetSim)
  - Cloud: ~6 tools (K8sOps, ServiceMesh, CostExplorer, CloudAudit, MultiCloud, EdgeProvision)
  - Other sectors: 4–5 tools each

**Public layer**:
- 5 domains: AI R&D, Product & Software, Hardware, Product Digitization, Infrastructure
- Total ~6–8 PDTs per domain (e.g., AI R&D has 6: SysDesign, DevServices, TestServices, R&DMaint, AIProdLine, KnowledgeServices)
- ~50+ tools distributed across domains

**MCP count**:
- 108 tool definitions in `MCP_TOOLS` array
- **41 real MCPs** across those tools (some tools have 0, some have 2–3)
- Placeholder synthesis: tools with `mcps: []` get a single placeholder tile at render time, so visible count is ~108 tiles per layer

**Total visible on panorama no-drill**: ~149 tiles (108 + ~41 orphan placeholders, rough estimate).

---

## What "No Drill" Structurally Means

### Current state without drilling:

URL: `/mcp/panorama` (no query params)
- `primary = null`, `secondary = null` (computed in usePanoramaState.ts, lines 28–30)
- `filteredGroups` computed includes all groups and all their tools (lines 72–95 in panorama.vue)
- PanoramaView renders ALL sector/domain cards in a single responsive grid
- No card is hidden or collapsed

### Would removing drill entirely change anything visually?

**No, not fundamentally.** The current "no drill" state *already shows everything*. Removing drill would mean:

1. **Remove CardHeader click handler** (currently emits `@drill`) — the group names would no longer be clickable
2. **Remove drill state from URL** — `primary` and `secondary` query params become unused
3. **Remove the drill-filter logic** (lines 60–64 in panorama.vue, the `inDrill()` function)
4. **UI would look identical** when landed with no drill

The only difference would be that the user can't collapse/re-expand groups. **The default experience is already "everything visible."**

---

## Structural Implications of "No Drill" Redesign

If we flatten drill entirely, these components would **simplify**:

1. **PanoramaView**: Still responsive grid of cards; still renders all groups
2. **SectorCard / DomainCard**: CardHeader would no longer be clickable (remove `@drill`); the title becomes static text
3. **CardHeader**: Button → static `<h3>` span (no-op)
4. **Drill state removed from URL**: `usePanoramaState` no longer tracks primary/secondary; router.replace calls in `setDrill()` and `clearDrill()` become no-ops
5. **No visual collapse/expand**: Cards always render fully
6. **No "top 3 by release" drill buttons** in LayerSummary (lines 150–165 become irrelevant)

**No truncation or hiding issues to solve** — every MCP already renders in the no-drill state.

---

## Reasonable Redesign Interpretations

### Interpretation 1: **"Both Layers in One View (Side-by-Side or Stacked)"**

**Concept**: Instead of layer toggle in sidebar, show Public and Industry side-by-side or stacked vertically on a single panorama page.

**Tradeoffs**:
- **Pro**: Compare industry vs. public tools at a glance; see the full landscape in one view
- **Pro**: Removes the mental context-switch of switching layers in sidebar
- **Con**: Width explosion: even stacked, two responsively-sized grids might require a wider viewport or two-column layout
- **Con**: LayerSummary would need duplication or a unified "all-layers" stats card
- **Con**: Drill would need layer context (e.g., `primary=wireless` is ambiguous if both layers have same-keyed groups)
- **Complexity**: Moderate — mostly layout + state refactor; drill mechanics still work per-layer

**UI sketch**: 
```
[Layer Stats (All)]
[Sector Cards Grid] [Domain Cards Grid]
 (Industry 12×)        (Public 5×)
```

---

### Interpretation 2: **"Dense Matrix: Status × Hierarchy (Heatmap-Style)"**

**Concept**: Instead of cards with grouped MCPs, render a single dense matrix where:
- Rows = sectors/domains/PDTs (hierarchically nestable or flat)
- Columns = status buckets (none, dev, released) or individual MCPs
- Cells = colored dots or mini-tiles showing MCP presence + status

**Tradeoffs**:
- **Pro**: Extreme space efficiency; all 149 MCPs visible as tiny cells on a single screen (no scroll needed)
- **Pro**: Status patterns jump out (e.g., a column of reds = lagging sector)
- **Con**: Loses the "card" visual hierarchy; tool names only visible on hover or in a tooltip
- **Con**: Small touch targets; desktop-first experience
- **Con**: Drill pattern doesn't map cleanly (clicking a cell opens side panel, but there's no "drill into a row" action)
- **Complexity**: High — requires new data-viz component library; fundamentally different interaction model

**UI sketch**:
```
           none  dev  released
Wireless    🔴  🟠   🟢
Datacom     🔴  🟠   🟢
Cloud       🔴  🟠   🟢
...
AI R&D
  SysDesign  🔴  🟠   🟢
  DevServices 🔴 🟠  🟢
  ...
```

---

### Interpretation 3: **"Flat List with Inline Filters and Status Indicators"**

**Concept**: Replace card + grid structure with a flat scrollable table/list:
- One row per MCP (or per tool, with MCPs grouped inline)
- Columns: Hierarchy (sector/domain/PDT path), Tool name, MCP name, Status (pill), Release %, Tags
- Sortable and filterable by status, layer, owner, deps count

**Tradeoffs**:
- **Pro**: Scales infinitely (table is vertical scroll; cards have wrapping limits)
- **Pro**: Every MCP name + blurb visible inline (no need to open side panel)
- **Pro**: Familiar tabular UX; easy to sort/filter
- **Con**: Loses the visual hierarchy and "landscape" feel; becomes a database query UI
- **Con**: Blurbs take horizontal space; might need truncation or expansion cells
- **Con**: No "drill" concept; filtering replaces it
- **Complexity**: Moderate — table + sort/filter logic

**UI sketch**:
```
Sector/Domain | Tool          | MCP           | Status   | Release% | Deps | Tags
Wireless      | 5G-Sim        | linksim-mcp   | 🟢 REL   | 100%     | 12   | [sim] [rf]
Wireless      | RadioPlan     | propmap-mcp   | 🟢 REL   | 100%     | 7    | [planning]
Wireless      | SpectrumMgr   | spectrum-mcp  | 🟠 DEV   | —        | 4    | [spectrum]
...
```

---

## Summary

The panorama **already renders all MCPs in the default (no-drill) state**. The drill mechanic is a *collapse/expand* feature, not a hiding mechanism. Removing it would simplify CardHeader and navigation state, but wouldn't require any truncation-hiding fixes.

**The information-hiding points are**:
1. Full blurbs + tags only appear in the side panel (ToolDetailPanel)
2. Downstream deps visualization only in side panel
3. Owner context only in side panel

All **MCP names, statuses, and counts are visible in the panorama itself** — no truncation at tile or card level.

If you want "everything in one view, no drill required," the current landing page *already is* that for the chosen layer. The three interpretations above offer different visual reorganizations around that baseline.
```

## Approved Plan:
# MCP Panorama — One Page, Both Layers

## Context

The panorama at `/mcp/panorama` shows one layer at a time (Public *or* Industry) and uses a sidebar layer toggle plus a drill tree to navigate the ~149 tiles per layer. The user wants an "overall view" where the whole landscape is visible without needing to drill or toggle to find more information.

Concrete read of the gap:

- **Default no-drill state already shows every MCP** in the active layer with no truncation — drill is a *narrowing filter*, not a hide-and-reveal mechanism.
- What's actually hidden until interaction:
  - **The other layer** — switching Public ↔ Industry requires a sidebar/mobile-rail toggle.
  - **Per-MCP detail** (blurb, tags, endpoint, downstream deps) — lives in the slide-in `ToolDetailPanel` until the tile is clicked.

User picked: **stack both layers on one page; keep the slide-in panel for per-MCP detail**. Card-based layout from today is preserved. Long scroll is acceptable; per-MCP detail stays one click away.

## Approach

Render Industry and Public sections one above the other on the same `/mcp/panorama` page, each using the existing `<PanoramaView>` component with its own data. The page-level `<SectionHeader>` shrinks to the controls that *don't* depend on a single active layer (status filter, view-mode toggle); the layer toggle goes away. The sidebar's panorama section drops its layer toggle and reframes its drill tree as a unified scroll-anchor navigator over both layers.

Drill as a *filter* becomes optional — by default everything is visible; clicking a sidebar drill node scrolls the page to that card instead of narrowing the view. Backwards-compat for the `?layer=…` URL param: treated as a scroll-on-load hint, not a content filter.

The slide-in `ToolDetailPanel` is preserved unchanged. Status filter (`?status=…`) and view-mode toggle (`?view=…`) keep their current URL-driven behavior — they apply globally to both layers' sections.

## Files to modify

### Core page

1. **`app/pages/mcp/panorama.vue`**
   - Run **two parallel** `useFetch<LayerPayload>("/api/internal/mcp-landscape", …)` calls with `query: { layer: "industry" }` and `query: { layer: "public" }`. Keep different cache keys (`mcp-landscape-industry`, `mcp-landscape-public`) so they don't collide.
   - Compute `filteredGroups` per layer using the existing `passesStatus` logic, but drop the `inDrill` filter (drill no longer narrows the visible groups).
   - Drop the `setLayer`, `setDrill`, `clearDrill`, `drillTo` paths from the script setup — `usePanoramaState` shrinks to `{ status, viewMode, setStatus, toggleStatus, setView }` for this page (see usePanoramaState change below).
   - Template:
     - `<SectionHeader>` once at the top (page-level controls only — no layer, no drill breadcrumb).
     - `<section id="layer-industry">` containing the Industry layer's `<PanoramaView>`.
     - `<section id="layer-public">` containing the Public layer's `<PanoramaView>`.
     - `<ToolDetailPanel>` last (unchanged).
   - On first mount: if `route.query.layer === "industry"` or `"public"`, `el.scrollIntoView()` the matching section after mount. Then strip the query param via `router.replace` so the URL canonicalizes to `/mcp/panorama`.

### Sidebar

2. **`app/components/mcp-landscape/PanoramaSidebarSection.vue`**
   - Drop the Industry/Public layer toggle pills.
   - Run **two** `useFetch<LayerPayload>(...)` calls with the same cache keys as the page (deduped by Nuxt).
   - Render a unified tree: an "Industry" heading with all industry sectors, then a "Public" heading with all domains + PDTs.
   - Click handler changes from `setDrill(…)` to scroll-to-anchor: each row links to `#group-<key>` (industry sectors) or `#group-<key>` / `#pdt-<domainKey>-<pdtKey>` (public). The relevant card root needs a matching `:id`.
   - Active-row highlighting via `IntersectionObserver` (scroll-spy) is *out of scope*; the rows are uniformly styled. Can revisit if needed.

3. **`app/components/mcp-landscape/SectionHeader.vue`**
   - Remove the mobile layer-toggle block at the top of the template (no longer applicable — layer toggle is gone on this page).
   - Remove the `layer` prop and the `update:layer` emit.
   - Remove the drill-breadcrumb block at the top of the title section (no active drill to clear).
   - Subtitle uses combined counts: `visibleCounts.total / totals.total` aggregated across both layers (page does the sum and passes in).

### Card components — add anchor IDs

4. **`app/components/mcp-landscape/SectorCard.vue`** — add `:id="\`group-${group.key}\`"` to the `<article>` root so PanoramaSidebarSection rows can scroll-link.

5. **`app/components/mcp-landscape/DomainCard.vue`** — same `:id="\`group-${group.key}\`"` on the root.

6. **`app/components/mcp-landscape/PdtBlock.vue`** — add `:id="\`pdt-${ownerDomain}-${pdt.key}\`"`. Needs a small prop to receive the parent domain's key.

7. **`app/components/mcp-landscape/CardHeader.vue`** — no behavior change today, but the drill-trigger button is now visually misleading. **Stop emitting** `@drill` (or no-op the click); the header becomes a plain `<h3>`. Drill is no longer a filtering mechanism.

8. **`app/components/mcp-landscape/PanoramaView.vue`** — stop forwarding `@drill` events (parent ignores them anyway). `LayerSummary`'s "Top 3 drill" buttons (lines 150–165 in LayerSummary) also become scroll-to-anchor links rather than drill emits.

9. **`app/components/mcp-landscape/LayerSummary.vue`** — `Top 3 by release` buttons change from `@click="emit('drill', g.key)"` to NuxtLink-style anchor scrolls (`href="#group-${g.key}"` or programmatic `scrollIntoView`). No more `drill` emit.

### State composable

10. **`app/composables/usePanoramaState.ts`**
    - Remove `primary`, `secondary`, `setDrill`, `clearDrill`, `toggleStatus`'s coupling to drill-clear. Keep `status`, `viewMode`, `setStatus`, `toggleStatus`, `setView`.
    - Keep `layer` and `setLayer` for backwards compat (URL param still parseable) — but mark `setLayer` as scroll-only and have it call `scrollIntoView` rather than mutate state for the panorama page.
    - Actually cleaner: drop `layer` and `setLayer` from the composable entirely; the panorama page reads `route.query.layer` once on mount for the scroll hint, then strips it. Other consumers (`/mcp` listing) don't need layer state. **Decision**: remove `layer/setLayer/primary/secondary/setDrill/clearDrill` from the composable. Page handles the scroll hint inline.

### Tests

11. **`app/components/layout/Sidebar.nuxt.test.ts`** — the "on /mcp/panorama" test asserts `aria-current=page` on "By system" and that FUNC_TAXONOMY is hidden. That still holds — the change is in `PanoramaSidebarSection`'s internals, not the Sidebar shell. No update needed.

12. **No new dedicated tests** for the page restructure itself — the rendering is just two PanoramaView instances and the data flow already has test coverage at the composable/middleware level. Add a small smoke check in the existing Sidebar test file: when on `/mcp/panorama`, no layer-toggle buttons exist in the sidebar (regression guard against the dropped toggle).

## What stays unchanged

- `/api/internal/mcp-landscape` server endpoint — same shape, same `?layer=` query.
- `shared/mcp-panorama.ts`, `shared/data/mcp-landscape.ts` — data types and seeds unchanged.
- `ToolDetailPanel.vue` — slide-in remains the per-MCP detail surface.
- The Sidebar's "Browse MCP" peer pills (`By function` / `By system`). The sidebar's bottom section still swaps between FUNC_TAXONOMY (on `/mcp`) and PanoramaSidebarSection (on `/mcp/panorama`), just with PanoramaSidebarSection's internals refactored.
- Decision #11 (accent restraint), decision #3 (single-row filter rail) — unaffected.
- Status filter URL semantics (`?status=released` etc.) — work identically; apply to both layers' sections simultaneously.
- View-mode toggle (`?view=panorama|list`) — applies to both layers' sections.

## Layer order

Industry first (top), Public second (bottom). Industry is the more org-internal lens; Public is the cross-domain catalog. Putting Industry first matches the existing sidebar order (Industry button precedes Public).

## Verification

Run `bun run dev`, then walk through:

1. `/en/mcp/panorama` — page loads with both Industry (12 sectors) and Public (5 domains + PDTs) sections. Scroll the whole page to confirm every sector/domain card is fully rendered with all tools and MCP tiles inline.
2. **Sidebar** — no layer toggle visible. The drill tree shows two headings ("Industry" / "Public") with all sectors/domains/PDTs underneath. Click an item → page scrolls smoothly to the matching card.
3. **Status filter** (`?status=released`) — both layers' sections re-render with only released MCPs; counts in each section's `LayerSummary` reflect the filter.
4. **View toggle** (`?view=list`) — both layers switch to GroupedListView.
5. **MCP click** — slide-in `ToolDetailPanel` opens with the detail of the clicked MCP, regardless of which layer the tile belongs to. Close the panel; main view unchanged.
6. **Legacy URLs**:
   - `/en/mcp/panorama?layer=industry` — page loads, scrolls Industry section into view, then URL strips to `/en/mcp/panorama`.
   - `/en/mcp-panorama` (older URL) — still redirected by `legacy-categories.global.ts` to `/en/mcp/panorama`. Behavior unchanged.
7. **Mobile** — `<md` viewport. No layer toggle in `SectionHeader`. Status chips, view toggle, and the slide-in panel work. Sidebar is hidden; user navigates by scrolling.
8. **Bilingual** — `/zh/mcp/panorama` renders both layers with Chinese labels (`Industry` → `行业`, etc.). Sidebar drill-tree headings render in Chinese.
9. `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` — all green.

## Branch & commit

Branch from latest `main`: `refactor/mcp-panorama-both-layers`. Two commits:

```
refactor(mcp-panorama): render both layers on one page
refactor(mcp-panorama): drill becomes scroll-to-anchor; drop drill state
```

The first does the heavy lifting (two fetches, two PanoramaView instances, SectionHeader/sidebar refactor); the second removes the now-unused drill plumbing from `usePanoramaState` and the card components.

## Out of scope

- **Scroll-spy active-section highlighting** in the sidebar — could be added later via `IntersectionObserver`; not needed for the v1 of this redesign.
- **Combined "all layers" summary stat card** at the top — instead each layer's `LayerSummary` (Activation %, top 3, etc.) renders inside its own section. Combining would be more work and the per-layer view is more informative.
- **Inline per-MCP detail in tiles** — full blurb/tags/endpoint stay in the slide-in panel. User explicitly picked the "keep side panel" option.
- **Replacing card layout with a denser table/matrix** — different redesign direction; can revisit if scroll depth becomes a real problem.
- **Promoting `/mcp/panorama` to a default landing** or changing the top-level sidebar pill behavior — the route stays `/mcp/panorama`, reached via the "By system" pill from `/mcp`. No change to navigation entry points.

 <SectionHeader\n      v-if=\"industryData || publicData\"\n      :visible-counts=\"visibleCounts\"\n      :totals=\"totals\"\n      :status-filter=\"statusFilter\"\n      :view-mode=\"viewMode\"\n ```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/app/composables/usePanoramaState.ts",
  "content": "import type { McpStatus } from \"~~/shared/data/mcp-landscape\"\n\nconst STATUSES = [\"all\", \"released\", \"dev\", \"none\"] as const\nconst VIEWS = [\"panorama\", \"list\"] as const\n\nexport type StatusFilter = (typeof STATUSES)[number]\nexport type ViewMode = (typeof VIEWS)[number]\n\nfunction parseEnum<T extends readonly string[]>(\n  value: unknown,\n  allowed: T,\n  fallback: T[number],\n): T[number] {\n  if (typeof value !== \"string\") return fallback\n  return (allowed as readonly string[]).includes(value) ? (value as T[number]) : fallback\n}\n\nexport function usePanoramaState() {\n  const route = useRoute()\n  const router = useRouter()\n\n  const status = computed<StatusFilter>(() => parseEnum(route.query.status, STATUSES, \"all\"))\n  const viewMode = computed<ViewMode>(() => parseEnum(route.query.view, VIEWS, \"panorama\"))\n\n  function push(partial: Record<string, string | null>) {\n    const merged: Record<string, string | null> = {}\n    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(route.query)) {\n      if (typeof v === \"string\") merged[k] = v\n    }\n    Object.assign(merged, partial)\n    const next: Record<string, string> = {}\n    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(merged)) {\n      if (v !== null) next[k] = v\n    }\n    router.replace({ path: route.path, query: next })\n  }\n\n  function setStatus(value: StatusFilter) {\n    push({ status: value === \"all\" ? null : value })\n  }\n\n  function toggleStatus(value: McpStatus) {\n    push({ status: status.value === value ? null : value })\n  }\n\n  function setView(value: ViewMode) {\n    push({ view: value === \"panorama\" ? null : value })\n  }\n\n  return {\n    status,\n    viewMode,\n    setStatus,\n    toggleStatus,\n    setView,\n  }\n}\n"
}
